newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - Sharp 1st half lift seen for FCL Energy.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Sharp 1st half lift seen for FCL Energy.

text.p: Strong oil prices over the last six months of 1996 are likely to translate into a sharply higher first half profit for Fletcher Energy, analysts said on Monday.
Most analysts are expecting a net profit, before an abnormal gain of NZ$32 million, of NZ$100 million compared with a NZ$20 net profit in the six months to December 1995.
The abnormal gain came from the sale of FCL Energy's holding in Bay of Plenty Electricity to Power New Zealand in July.
While a higher New Zealand dollar will have a dampening effect, analysts expect the spike up in crude prices to be the most dominant feature.

"It's going to be hugely up on last year's result but it's probably mostly anticipated," Guy Hallwright at First NZ Capital said. Hallwright said that on top of strong oil prices, FCL Energy would stand to gain from increased production from the Maui B offshore field coming on stream in the half year.
Over the period, prices for Asia Pacific tapis rose about six U.S. dollars a barrel to US$26.20 by the end of last year.

Kevin O'Connor at Doyle Paterson Brown expects a net profit before abnormal items of just under NZ$100 million, but he saw big costs coming from depreciation, depletion and amortisation from the oil and gas fields.

FCL Energy shares have performed strongly over the last six months, but have recently gone through a flat period. They closed on Monday at NZ$3.95, down five cents, against a year high of NZ$4.34 and a low of $2.83.

Little more information is expected to come from FCL Energy when it reports on Wednesday, the company having already reported its latest production numbers and published an update on progress with its Brunei field.
Total production for the December quarter was 11.3 million barrels of oil equivalent, 18 percent up on the same period in 1995.

Production of liquids increased by 47 percent, reflecting the successful commissioning of the Floating Production and Storage Offloading Vessel Whakaaropai. FCL Energy's share of production averaged 18,467 barrels per day.
Onshore NZ the Manu-1 and Mangahewa-2 wells both encountered gas in their respective target zones. The Manu well has been temporarily suspended while Mangahewa is still being drilled.
Analysts said Mangahewa was looking promising but that it would take time to establish commercial viability.
In December, FCL Energy and its partners said they had decided to proceed with development of the Maharaja Lela gas and condensate field, offshore from Brunei Darussalam.
FCL Energy owns 35 percent and other shareholders include Elf Aquitaine (37.5 poercent), Bruneian company JASRA (22.5 percent and other Bruneian interests (five percent).
